program.name: Lime
program.title: QA & Testing Knowledge Portal
program.tagline: How testing works on the {{program}} Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP program.
program.overview: {{program}} is implementing Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP for its quote-to-cash and related financial processes. This portal is the single place to learn how testing works on the program, find templates and criteria, and see how the testing dashboard is defined. It is a reference site: it does not connect to live Jira or ALM, but it can load exports from them.

resultStatuses.def: Executed and the actual result matched the expected result.
Executed and the actual result did not match the expected result.
Could not be completed because of a defect, data or environment dependency.
Not yet executed. Never counted as Passed.
Execution has started but no result is recorded yet.
Removed from the planned scope for this cycle. Excluded from rates and never counted as Passed.

objectives: Confirm that the Oracle Fusion Cloud ERP solution meets the agreed business requirements before go-live.
Find and fix defects early, in the cycle where they are cheapest to fix.
Give business users enough evidence to accept the solution and sign off.
Give program leadership a trustworthy, consistently defined view of testing status.
principles: Results are reported separately for FUT/TUT, SIT and UAT.
Every result is backed by evidence that someone else can review.
Every failed or blocked script is linked to a defect or has a documented disposition.
Missing data is shown as missing. It is never counted as zero or as passed.
Entry and exit criteria are checked before a cycle starts and before it closes.
Thresholds and definitions come from the program configuration, not from individual judgment.

lifecycle.name: Plan
lifecycle.text: Agree scope, cycles, criteria and roles.

lifecycle.name: Design
lifecycle.text: Write scripts and trace them to user stories and RICE objects.

lifecycle.name: Prepare
lifecycle.text: Ready the environment, data, security access and testers.

lifecycle.name: Execute
lifecycle.text: Run scripts, capture evidence and record results.

lifecycle.name: Manage defects
lifecycle.text: Log, triage, fix, re-test and close defects.

lifecycle.name: Report
lifecycle.text: Calculate KPIs and apply RAG rules for each cycle.

lifecycle.name: Close and sign off
lifecycle.text: Confirm exit criteria and record acceptance.

strategy.keyRule: FUT/TUT, SIT, and UAT results are reported separately and never merged into one pass rate unless the definitions are comparable.

security.intro: Security and access are readiness dependencies for testing. They are tracked as dependencies, not as test results, unless an explicit test record exists.

topics.text: Defines which user groups need which access in each environment.
Confirms that role combinations do not create conflicting duties.
Job and duty roles are built, assigned and reviewed against the access design.
Users can reach only the data they are meant to see and change.
Testers and business users receive their access before each cycle starts.
After an environment refresh, confirm that users, roles and access are restored or re-applied. Confirm the exact steps with the project team.
Access needed during mock cutovers and the production cutover is defined and approved.

statuses.text: Logged and waiting for triage or assignment.
Assigned and being analyzed or fixed.
Fix delivered and waiting for re-test.
Re-test failed or the issue recurred. Returns to the fix queue.

severities.text: Stops testing or a business-critical process with no workaround, or puts financial accuracy or compliance at risk.
severities.example: Invoices cannot be generated, or revenue posts to the wrong period.

severities.text: A major function fails or gives wrong results. A workaround exists but is difficult or risky.
severities.example: Tax is calculated incorrectly for one customer group.

severities.text: A function partly fails or gives a wrong result. An acceptable workaround exists.
severities.example: A report total is correct but a subtotal is missing.

severities.text: A minor issue with no effect on results.

priorities.text: Fix immediately. The defect blocks the cycle or a critical process.
Fix within the current cycle window.
Fix before the cycle exits, or agree a deferral.
Fix when capacity allows. May be deferred with approval.

requiredFields.why: Lets anyone find and recognize the defect in a list.
Lets the fixer see the same problem.
Shows what is wrong and what correct looks like.
Drives the order of work and the escalation path.
Needed for Defect Density and Defect Leakage by cycle.
Needed for coverage and for routing to the right owner.
Separates data problems from configuration problems.
Screenshots or logs prove the result without a conversation.
Needed for aging and for follow-up questions.

goodDefect: Write a summary that names the object and the problem, for example: "Invoice total excludes tax for order type X".
List the exact steps, the data used and the user role you used.
State the expected result and the actual result separately.
Attach a screenshot or log that shows the problem.
Link the defect to the failed script and the user story.
Set severity from the business impact, not from how hard the fix looks.

nodes.label: User story
nodes.text: The requirement or change that the test is meant to prove.

nodes.label: Test script
nodes.text: The scripted steps and expected results that cover a story.

nodes.label: Execution
nodes.text: One run of a script by a named tester in a cycle.

nodes.label: Result
nodes.text: Passed, Failed, Blocked, Not Run, In Progress or Not Applicable.

nodes.label: Defect
nodes.text: A logged problem linked to the failed or blocked script and to its story.

gaps.title: Stories without scripts
gaps.text: A story has no linked test script, so nothing proves it works.
gaps.fix: Write or link a script, or mark the story out of scope with approval.

gaps.title: Failed tests without defects
gaps.text: A script failed but no defect explains why.
gaps.fix: Log a defect and link it to the script, or record a documented disposition.

gaps.title: Defects without stories
gaps.text: A defect cannot be traced back to the requirement it affects.
gaps.fix: Link the defect to the correct story, or log a new story for gaps in the requirements.

gaps.title: Missing process, module or RICE mapping
gaps.text: Records without these fields cannot be grouped, filtered or routed to an owner.
gaps.fix: Add the missing fields in the source system and re-load the data.

kpis.name: Execution %
kpis.definition: Share of planned, applicable scripts that have been executed to a result.
kpis.denominator: Passed + Failed + Blocked + Not Run + In Progress
kpis.exclusions: Not Applicable scripts are excluded from the denominator.
kpis.source: Test execution records (Jira, Excel fallback, or ALM adapter required)

outputs.label: Execution %
outputs.denLabel: Passed + Failed + Blocked + Not Run + In Progress

kpis.name: Pass / Fail / Block rate
kpis.definition: Share of executed results that are Passed, Failed or Blocked. Reported separately for each cycle.
kpis.numerator: Count of the result being measured
kpis.exclusions: Not Run, In Progress and Not Applicable are excluded. Not Run and Not Applicable are never counted as Passed.
kpis.source: Test execution records (Jira, Excel fallback, or ALM adapter required)

kpis.name: First-Pass Yield
kpis.definition: Share of executed scripts that passed on the first attempt.
kpis.exclusions: Scripts not yet executed and Not Applicable scripts.
kpis.source: Execution records that include an attempt number

kpis.name: Re-test Pass Rate
kpis.definition: Share of re-executed scripts that passed.
kpis.denominator: Re-executed scripts with a result (attempt 2 or later: Passed + Failed + Blocked)
kpis.exclusions: First-attempt executions; scripts not yet re-executed.
kpis.source: Execution records that include an attempt number

kpis.name: Coverage %
kpis.definition: Share of in-scope user stories that have at least one linked test script in the cycle.
kpis.numerator: Stories with at least one linked script in the cycle
kpis.exclusions: Stories formally marked out of scope.

inputs.label: Stories with at least one linked script

kpis.name: Defect Density
kpis.definition: Defects found relative to the volume of executed testing, expressed per 100 executed scripts.
kpis.exclusions: Defects rejected as invalid; scripts not yet executed.

kpis.name: Defect Aging
kpis.definition: Average number of days that open defects have been open. Bucket counts are shown on the Defect Management page.
kpis.numerator: Sum of days open across all open defects

inputs.label: Sum of days open across open defects

kpis.name: Defect Leakage
kpis.definition: Share of defects found in a cycle that should have been caught in an earlier cycle.
kpis.numerator: Defects found in the cycle and attributed to an earlier cycle
kpis.denominator: All defects found in the cycle
kpis.exclusions: Not applicable to FUT/TUT because no earlier cycle exists.
kpis.source: Defect records with an 'escaped from' attribution

inputs.label: Defects attributed to an earlier cycle
All defects found in the cycle

outputs.label: Defect Leakage
outputs.denLabel: All defects found in the cycle

kpis.name: Data Completeness %
kpis.definition: Share of expected source records that are converted, validated and supported by evidence.
kpis.source: Data conversion status and record counts

rag.intro: Each metric is rated Green, Amber or Red by comparing its value with thresholds from the program configuration. The logic never contains a number of its own.

definitions.text: The value is on the target side of the Green threshold. No action is needed beyond normal monitoring.
The value has passed the Green threshold but has not reached the Red threshold. An owner and a recovery action are required.
The value is beyond the Amber threshold. Escalate to the program manager and record a decision.
No threshold is set for this metric, or the metric is Not Available. The portal never guesses a rating.

activities: Define the test strategy and cycles
Provision tester and business user access
Accept results and sign off UAT

tester.title: Before you test
steps: Confirm that the cycle has started and that its entry criteria are met.
Check that you can sign in with the role assigned to the script.
Open the script and read the preconditions and test data.
Confirm the environment is the one named in the script.
Raise any gap before you start: missing access, missing data or an unclear step.

tester.title: Run a script
steps: Follow the steps in order. Do not skip or combine steps.
Compare the actual result with the expected result at each step.
Record the result for the script: Passed, Failed or Blocked.
If a step cannot be completed, stop and mark the script Blocked. Link the reason.
Mark a script Not Applicable only with approval from the QA lead.

tester.title: Capture evidence
steps: Take a screenshot at each point that proves an expected result.
Show the record number, the date and your user in the screenshot where possible.
Attach evidence to the execution record, not to an email.
Name files so that a reviewer can match them to the script and step.

tester.title: Log a defect
steps: Search existing defects first to avoid duplicates.
Use the defect template and complete every required field.
Set severity from business impact and propose a priority.
Link the defect to the script and the user story.
Link the defect ID back to the failed or blocked execution.

tester.title: Re-test
steps: Wait for the defect to reach Resolved.
Re-run the full script, not only the failed step.
Record the new attempt. The attempt number increases by one.
If it passes, move the defect to Closed. If it fails, move it to Reopened and add the new evidence.

tester.title: Hand over results
steps: Check that every executed script has a result, a date and evidence.
Check that every Failed or Blocked script has a defect or a documented disposition.
Give the QA lead your completed records before the daily status deadline.

uat.title: Before you start
steps: Make sure you have your sign-in and that you can open the test system.
Open the scripts assigned to you. Each script is one business task to try.
Ask your UAT lead if anything is unclear. Do not guess.
Have your sample data ready. Your UAT lead will tell you where to find it.

uat.title: Run a script
steps: Do each step in the script in order.
After each step, check: did the system do what the script said it would?
If yes, carry on. If no, stop and note exactly what happened.
At the end, mark the script Passed, Failed or Blocked.

uat.title: Capture evidence
steps: Take a screenshot when the screen shows the result you were asked to check.
Add a short comment about what you saw, especially if anything looked unusual.
Attach the screenshot to your script record.

uat.title: Report a problem
steps: Tell your UAT lead or log a defect using the template.
Say what you did, what you expected and what you saw.
Attach your screenshot.
Mark the script Failed, or Blocked if you could not finish it.

uat.title: Re-test after a fix
steps: You will be told when the problem is fixed.
Run the whole script again.
Record the new result and add new evidence.

uat.title: Accept and sign off
steps: Accept a script only when the result matches what your business needs.
Add a comment to explain any condition on your acceptance.
When all your scripts are done, complete the UAT sign-off form with your authorized approver.
Sign-off means the business accepts the solution for the scope tested. Outstanding items must be listed.

items: I can sign in to the UAT environment.
I know which scripts are assigned to me.
I have my test data and my role.
I know who my UAT lead is.
I followed each step in order.
I recorded Passed, Failed or Blocked for every script.
I attached a screenshot as evidence.
I added a comment where something looked unusual.
I reported every problem as a defect or to my UAT lead.
I re-ran the whole script after each fix.
I recorded the new result and new evidence.
Every assigned script has a result and a comment.
Outstanding items are listed with an agreed owner.
The authorized approver has signed the UAT sign-off form.

rules.rule: Every test result has a cycle that maps to a configured cycle.
rules.fix: Add or correct the cycle in the source, or add the spelling to the cycle aliases in the configuration.

rules.rule: Every status value maps to a known status.
rules.fix: Correct the status in the source, or add the spelling to the status aliases in the configuration.

rules.rule: A test ID appears only once per cycle.
rules.fix: Remove the duplicate rows or keep only the latest result per script.

rules.rule: Every Passed, Failed or Blocked result has an execution date.
rules.fix: Record the execution date in the source system.

rules.rule: Every Failed or Blocked result is linked to a defect, or has a documented disposition.
rules.fix: Log a defect and link it, or record the disposition.

rules.rule: Every defect is linked to a user story.
rules.fix: Link the defect to its story in the source system.

rules.rule: Every in-scope story has at least one test script.
rules.fix: Write or link a script, or mark the story out of scope with approval.

rules.rule: Records carry a module and a process. RICE ID is expected only where a RICE object is involved.
rules.fix: Fill in the missing fields in the source system and re-load.

rules.rule: Dates can be read and are not in the future.
rules.fix: Correct the date format in the source, for example 2026-09-14.

rules.rule: No conversion step is marked Complete without evidence.
rules.fix: Attach the evidence reference or change the step status.

faq.q: Why are FUT/TUT, SIT and UAT never combined into one pass rate?
faq.a: They use different data, different testers and different goals. A combined rate would hide the real status of each cycle. Combine them only when the definitions are comparable and the combined figure is labeled.

faq.q: Does Not Run count as a failure or as a pass?
faq.a: Neither. Not Run is excluded from the pass, fail and block rates. It lowers Execution %.

faq.q: What if a metric cannot be calculated?
faq.a: The portal shows Not Available with the reason, for example a zero denominator or missing source data. It never shows zero for missing data.

faq.q: Can I load data from Jira or ALM?
faq.a: Yes, from exports. Open Data sources and integration, choose the Import data tab and map your columns. A direct live connection is not included. ALM-specific details are marked ALM adapter required.
From portal-config.json. Entry and exit thresholds and RAG thresholds are read from it. Any threshold that is not set shows To be confirmed by project team.

faq.q: What is the difference between severity and priority?
faq.a: Severity is the business impact of the defect. Priority is how soon it should be fixed.

faq.q: Is security access a test result?
faq.a: No. It is a readiness dependency unless an explicit test record exists.

faq.q: How do I add a module or a cycle?
faq.a: Edit portal-config.json. See the instructions in the README. No page code needs to change.

faq.q: What does 'complete' mean for a data conversion step?
faq.a: A step is complete only when source evidence is recorded. A step marked Complete without evidence is shown as not counted.

faq.q: Is anything stored in my browser?
faq.a: No. The portal does not use localStorage or sessionStorage. Imported data lives in memory until you reload the page.

assumptions.text: The portal is a reference site. It reads exported files only and makes no live connection to Jira, ALM or any other system.
All sample content for the program called Lime is fictional and generic: processes, RICE object names, module links, criteria owners, RACI letters, glossary text and sample records.

Sample RAG thresholds exist for three metrics only (Execution %, Pass rate, average defect age) and are illustrative. Aging bucket boundaries are illustrative. All other thresholds, limits and SLAs are not set.
Execution % uses Passed + Failed + Blocked as the numerator and all planned, applicable scripts (Not Applicable excluded) as the denominator.
Defect Leakage is calculated for the receiving cycle: defects found in the cycle and attributed to an earlier cycle, divided by all defects found in the cycle.
Open defects are those with status Open, In Progress or Reopened. Resolved and Closed are not counted as open.
Status, severity, priority and cycle aliases (for example To Do mapped to Open) are generic and editable. Values that match no alias are flagged as unmapped, never guessed.
Sheet names and purposes for Testing_Daily_Status.xlsx are placeholders and must be confirmed against the real workbook.
The defect lifecycle transitions shown are generic and must be confirmed against the workflow in the defect source system.
Only the RICE complexity distribution (3 Simple, 6 Medium, 4 Complex, 7 Very Complex) comes from the scope. Object names, types and module links are illustrative.
'Clientes' in the conversion object list is treated as Customers and covered by Customer Master.
Vertex integration is treated as an integration / boundary application. How it is tested in each cycle is to be confirmed.
Severity and priority definitions and the severity/priority matrix are generic industry conventions, not Oracle- or client-specific rules.
First-Pass Yield and Re-test Pass Rate need an attempt number per result. Without it, they show Not Available.
ALM-specific connection details are not provided. Exports from ALM can be loaded as CSV or Excel files. A direct feed needs an ALM adapter.
Each test and defect row is assigned to a cycle through the cycle aliases. Rows that match no alias are reported as unmapped and are not merged into any cycle.
The portal is one HTML file that loads Chart.js and SheetJS from a public CDN. Open it with internet access. Open Sans loads from Google Fonts and falls back to Arial.
Imported data is held in memory only. Reloading the page returns to the configuration and sample data.
Imported dates are read in ISO format and common day-month-year formats. Unreadable dates are flagged and are not guessed.
Coverage % counts all loaded stories as in scope because no out-of-scope flag exists in the sample dictionary.
Entry and exit criteria owners and evidence names are illustrative. Thresholds are not set.
The escalation path levels and the roles in the RACI table are illustrative. Triggers are not set.
Fixed record counts for Customer Master and Product Master, conversion evidence references, and conversion step statuses are sample values.

Confirm the conversion object list, expected record counts and the evidence repository.
Confirm security design status, SoD approach and the pod refresh schedule.
Confirm the SIT business stakeholders and the UAT approvers.
Decide whether a regression cycle is needed and, if so, define it.
Confirm the escalation path, triggers and the RACI.

selfCheck: Navigation: open every page from the left menu. The page title changes and focus moves to the main heading.
Role path: choose each role in Start here. A numbered path appears and the links open the right pages.
Search: type 'denominator'. Results appear. Use the arrow keys and Enter to open one. Press Escape to close the list.
Filters: on Scope, RICE and Defects, change each filter. The row counts update and Clear filters restores them.
Calculator: on Metrics, calculate Pass rate with Passed 25, Failed 3, Blocked 2, Not Run 10. Expect 83.3% with denominator 30.
Missing data: clear one input in the calculator. Expect Not Available with a reason, not 0.
Zero denominator: enter 0 for Passed, Failed and Blocked. Expect Not Available.
Import: load a file from the sample-imports folder. The data banner changes and the pages update.
Modal: open a KPI or template. Press Escape. The dialog closes and focus returns to the button.
Copy and print: copy a template and paste it elsewhere. Print a template and the UAT checklist.
Keyboard only: tab through a page. Focus is always visible and nothing is skipped or trapped.
Contrast and zoom: zoom to 200% and check the layout. Check that status chips show text as well as color.
Storage: confirm in browser tools that localStorage and sessionStorage are empty.
